name: Do ADU bathrooms need special waterproofing in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What waterproofing details are most important in an ADU bathroom in Southern California?
mainEntity.text: What waterproofing details are most important in an ADU bathroom in Southern California?

acceptedAnswer.text: ADU bathrooms need standard bathroom waterproofing done carefully, especially around showers, tubs, and any floor or wall penetrations. The shower pan, curb, niches, bench areas, and lower walls are the most leak-prone parts of the room. In a compact ADU bathroom, even a small leak can cause damage quickly because everything is packed tightly together and repairs may require opening finished surfaces. Waterproofing details should be coordinated before tile starts, not improvised in the field. Homeowners should ask what system is being used, how corners and seams are sealed, and how the contractor tests the shower before tile installation. It is also smart to verify that the bathroom floor slopes and transitions are handled correctly so water stays in the wet zone. In Los Angeles-area projects, a luxury finish does not matter if the waterproofing is weak. A proper waterproofing plan protects the investment and reduces the chance of future callbacks or mold issues.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, ADU bathrooms need proper waterproofing anywhere water can reach the framing, subfloor, and slab. That includes the shower pan, shower walls, tub surround, floor transitions, and any areas around penetrations. Good waterproofing is especially important in compact bathrooms because leaks spread faster in tight layouts.
